‘Bi-Merge’ Proposal Threatens Core Mortgage Data Volumes
The primary driver behind the decline in EFX shares is Pulte’s explicit warning that the FHFA is “seriously considering bi-merge” credit reporting and “stronger solutions”.

Under the traditional “tri-merge” model, mortgage lenders are required to pull credit files from all three bureaus—Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, for every home loan delivered to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.

Shifting to a bi-merge framework would allow lenders to pull reports from only two bureaus, effectively removing one-third of total mortgage report volume across the industry and creating substantial structural revenue headwinds for Equifax.
